items.title: 67849_Leroy Elliot Stewart oral history interview
items.q: especially Roy and myself one night, if I remember, got into -- just the two of us -- and we got into this session

ctx.x: Now, did you work much with Roy Eldridge on 52nd Street during those years?

Not very much. He used to come in also and sit in with Art Tatum and myself and, of course, I got into quite a few sessions in after-hour places uptown, you know, especially Roy and myself one night, if I remember, got into -- just the two of us -- and we got into this session somewhat like a Don Byas and Slam Stewart affair, you know, and we just blew and blew for up to an hour, just the two of us.

items.title: 61530_Roy Eldridge oral history interview
items.q: I told Slam, I said, "When we go back on, we're not going on the bandstand."

ctx.x: So I said to myself, "I'm not gonna get in no argument with this cat. I told Slam, I said, "When we go back on, we're not going on the bandstand." I said, "Just bring the bass and follow me." I went to the bar, and Slam played at the bar, and then we played to the tables until the set was over. We did that the next set, and he got the message then. I wasn't about be playing with him (?), you know. And the next night, Panama was there; Zutty didn't show no more.
Well, I had no choice, man! And I liked Zutty, you know. But he just...
